title: Arkhaven private gateway readiness discovery
summary: Discovery call to map Arkhaven's private/VPC deployment constraints and readiness for a Redwood Private pilot. Focus on VPC peering vs Private Endpoint options, egress controls, region restrictions, and security requirements (KMS, audit logs, SSO). Agreed to a technical deep dive and exchange of network diagrams and SOC2 docs.
topics: Egress controls and country-based region gating
Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC
action_items: Lena Park | Send SOC2 + security pack and network checklist | 2027-10-21
Daniel Ortiz | Schedule SE deep dive and prepare private endpoint example diagrams | 2027-10-22
Maya Singh | Share current VPC CIDR ranges and peering constraints (Transit GW account IDs) | 2027-10-20
next_steps: Redwood to email security artifacts and onboarding checklist
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) for next week
Customer to provide VPC diagram and egress policy doc
Agree pilot region (eu-west-1 preferred) and test account access
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Arkhaven Head of Infra), Tom Becker (Arkhaven Security), Priya Raman (Arkhaven Platform)

Summary: quick intro, goals for pilot, networking constraints, security & compliance checklist, next steps

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Lena, I'll run the intro, Daniel from SE is here. Quick around the room, Maya?
[00:14] Maya Singh: Hey, Maya here. We're looking to evaluate private deployment options for low-latency internal APIs. Main ask is we need a model runtime inside our VPC or private link - no public egress for inference traffic.
[00:28] Daniel Ortiz: Great, thanks Maya. Couple clarifying q's up front: are you leaning toward a peering/transit gateway model or private endpoints like PrivateLink/Private Service Connect?
[00:38] Priya Raman: We're considering both. Our infra team prefers transit gateway so we can centralize routing, but security keeps bringing up the private endpoint model because it avoids peering exposure.
[00:50] Tom Becker: Right, from security: we need strong egress controls, country-level region gating, and KMS integration for keys. SOC2 is table stakes. Also audit logs need to flow into our SIEM.
[01:05] Lena Park: Totally understandable. For context, Redwood Private supports both deployment topologies; we've seen customers use hub-and-spoke with transit gateway or private endpoint attachments. Each has tradeoffs for routing complexity and scaling.
[01:20] Daniel Ortiz: On the runtime side, we map requests to a private dataplane. For transit gateway you'd peer the subnet where the Redwood workers live into your hub; with Private Endpoints we expose an endpoint in your VPC that terminates into our infra — both can be done without public internet egress.
[01:39] Maya Singh: Can you remind us about IP planning? We have limited /16 space in our prod VPCs, and we can't overlap with other vendor subnets.
[01:50] Daniel Ortiz: Yep. For peering/hub patterns we ask for an isolated CIDR for the Redwood subnet, ideally a /22 or /21 depending on concurrency. For private endpoints less CIDR is needed but you'll need ENI IP capacity and route table entries.
[02:09] Tom Becker: What about NAT/bastion requirements? Our security policy says no outbound to internet except via central NAT in prod — does Redwood need outbound for updates or metrics?
[02:21] Lena Park: With Private deployments the control plane traffic can be routed over the management plane with a customer-controlled endpoint. For hosted telemetry we can stream over a private peering link; otherwise there's an option to proxy telemetry through your NAT. We document both patterns.
[02:40] Priya Raman: Region constraints: we operate in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. For data residency, we need inference to stay in eu-west-1 for EU customers. Can Redwood pin model hosting by region?
[02:53] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, we can pin model instances to region and enforce routing policies. For EU residency we would deploy the Redwood private nodes in eu-west-1 region only and route traffic there. We also support automatic fallback but that can be disabled for strict residency.
[03:12] Maya Singh: How do you handle secrets and keys? We use AWS KMS and HSM for keywrap. Does Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
[03:22] Daniel Ortiz: We support customer KMS integrations (customer-managed CMKs) via IAM roles and key policies; for HSM you can bring-your-own-key through our private deployment model. We'll need an IAM trust and least-privilege role for the node to decrypt model artifacts if you want that.
[03:40] Tom Becker: Audit logs — we need proof of model access, prompt logs redaction rules, and retention configurable. Can logs be forwarded to our Splunk/ELK?
[03:51] Lena Park: Yes, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We also provide token-level cost/latency telemetry but sensitive data can be redacted at capture time. Retention windows are configurable in Private.
[04:06] Priya Raman: Network walkthrough — we're a hub-and-spoke with central transit GW in account A, spokes in prod accounts. We prefer Redwood in a shared services VPC attached to the transit GW. Any blockers?
[04:18] Daniel Ortiz: That pattern works. We'll need the transit GW attachment and proper route tables. One thing to watch: if you use asymmetric routing with NAT in the hub, stateful flows may require specific SNAT handling. Also, if you plan cross-region peering, performance varies and we usually recommend regional placement to avoid inter-region egress costs.
[04:45] Maya Singh: Do you support PrivateLink in GCP or Azure equivalents? We have a multi-cloud footprint.
[04:53] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, we have analogs: Private Service Connect in GCP and Private Link in Azure. Implementation details differ but the concepts are similar — we'll provide cloud-specific diagrams in the SE deep dive.
[05:08] Tom Becker: How about certificate management for mTLS? We require mutual TLS between our services and vendor endpoints.
[05:16] Lena Park: mTLS is supported in Private; we can integrate your CA or accept certs via our onboarding process. We'll document rotation windows.
[05:27] Maya Singh: SLA expectations — if we go dedicated/reserved nodes, can we get latency SLOs?
[05:34] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Dedicated provides predictable throughput and we can agree on P99 latency targets in the contract. For Private deployments in your VPC with reserved capacity we can do similar commitments.
[05:46] Priya Raman: Cost concerns — our finance team will ask about egress and token-level unit economics. If we pin to eu-west-1 and keep everything internal, is egress still a big cost?
[05:58] Lena Park: Egress costs drop significantly if everything stays regional and on private links. The main driver then is instance sizing and quantization—our Optimize team will run workload profiling to show cost per 1k tokens. We'll share a sample spreadsheet.
[06:16] (crosstalk)
[06:20] Daniel Ortiz: One more technical note: KV cache and prefix caching—if you have multi-tenant traffic we can configure per-tenant cache sharding or pin workloads to dedicated nodes to avoid cold-starts.
[06:34] Maya Singh: For the pilot, what do you need from us to start?
[06:39] Lena Park: At minimum: VPC diagram, CIDR ranges, admin contacts, SOC2 or security questionnaire responses, and a list of test prompts or workloads so our Optimize team can size the instance.
[06:53] Priya Raman: Timeline — we want a pilot by end of November, about six weeks out. Is that reasonable?
[07:01] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, that should be feasible. SE deep dive this week, then we ingest your diagram and spin test nodes. Private endpoint or transit attachments typically take 1-2 weeks once network approvals are complete.
[07:16] Tom Becker: Any blockers for procurement? We have a standard security review — will you sign a DPA and provide necessary attestations?
[07:24] Lena Park: We can sign a DPA; we'll include SOC2 and any encryption attestations. For enterprise customers we have templates that legal can iterate on.
[07:36] Maya Singh: Edge case: we have a legacy on-prem datacenter that must remain isolated. Can Redwood nodes be placed in our private colo or do you require public cloud?
[07:47] Daniel Ortiz: Our Private on-prem package supports air-gapped or colo deployments, though it requires additional ops work and a slightly longer timeline. We'll flag that in the deep dive if you want to explore it.
[08:03] Priya Raman: Ok. Security detail: redaction of prompts - we have PII risk. Can Redwood do PII scrubbing before logs leave the VPC?
[08:14] Lena Park: Yes, we support configurable redaction hooks; for strict cases you can disable telemetry export and keep logs local to your SIEM.
[08:26] (brief pause)
[08:32] Daniel Ortiz: I'm going to call out a couple of follow-ups I'll prepare: cloud-specific private endpoint diagrams, recommended CIDR sizes for high-concurrency inference, and an example Transit GW route table.
[08:46] Maya Singh: Great. Also, can you include sample IAM policies for the roles needed to access KMS and S3 artifacts?
[08:55] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, I'll add sample least-privilege IAM policies to the doc pack.
[09:02] Lena Park: To recap: Redwood will send security pack + SOC2, SE will run a technical deep dive and deliver network diagrams, Arkhaven will share VPC CIDRs and egress policy, and we'll schedule the pilot for late November.
[09:18] Tom Becker: Sounds good. Any immediate risks we're missing?
[09:22] Priya Raman: Just internal approvals on our side — network team needs to sign off on CIDR allocation.
[09:29] Maya Singh: Also need procurement throttle — our vendor onboarding can take 2 weeks.
[09:33] Lena Park: We can align timelines. We'll send the checklist so you can start approvals in parallel.
[09:41] (audio glitch)
[09:46] Daniel Ortiz: Quick note — if you want to restrict automatic fallback we can turn it off so there is no cross-region failover for EU data.
[09:55] Maya Singh: Let's disable fallback for now.
[09:58] Lena Park: Noted. Any other questions?
[10:02] Tom Becker: One last: do you have a reference for a similar customer in regulated infra? We want to see a case study.
[10:09] Lena Park: We'll include a redacted reference and a short case study in the pack.
[10:14] Priya Raman: Cool, thanks everyone.
[10:17] Lena Park: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs.
[10:20] Meeting end.
